newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, Jordan to expand trade agreement.
newsitem.headline: Israel, Jordan to expand trade agreement.

text.p: Israel and Jordan will expand their trade agreement by granting preferential customs on a number of products not included in the original accord, Israel's Ministry of Industry and Trade said on Wednesday.
The two sides held the first meeting in Israel of a joint economic committee meant to address problems of implementation of the trade accord, which came into effect in March.
The head of the foreign trade administration at the Israeli ministry, Zohar Peri, said Israel was interested in improving trade ties between the countries.
Last October Israel and Jordan signed a trade agreement that included a list of products that would benefit from preferential duties.

The two sides decided in this week's talks to increase the number of products that would enjoy preferential customs. Each side will prepare a list to be presented for discussion and approval at a meeting of the trade ministers to be held soon.

Israel also raised the possibility of a free trade agreement, as was aimed for at the start of the peace negotiations between the two countries. The two countries signed a peace treaty in Octoer 1994.
At this week's meeting the Jordanians requested measures to facilitate the transport of goods between the two countries.
